newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 22.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

US President Bill Clinton yesterday outlined the values and crucial importance of racial tolerance in a powerful speech to the Australian nation. Clinton said that Australia was a great haven in the modern world, when many places still persecuted people only on the basis of racial difference. Australia he said, was being looked to by America and the rest of the world for racial leadership. Page 1.

Communications Minister Richard Alston yesterday agreed with backbenchers, forcing the telecommunications carriers Telstra and Optus to comply fully with local planning laws when they roll-out their overhead cable networks. The two companies will now have to fight many local councils who are already deeply opposed to the roll-out. Page 1.

A new forecasting system has been developed by Australian scientists and will be used by farmers, commodity analysts and water authorities to predict long-term weather patterns. The new system outlined in the latest edition of Nature advances the use
of te Southern Oscillation Index and provides a more accurate reading of the El Nino effect. Page 2.

The next APEC forum will take place this weekend in the Philippines for a crucial summit aimed at maintaining the momentum of trade reform. US President Bill Clinton is under a lot of pressure to reinvigorate APEC nations' commitment to the forum with new market opening initiatives. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

American President Bill Clinton believes Australia's efforts in building a multicultural society are a "shining example" for other nations trying to overcome intolerance. He said Sydney had an opportunity to serve as a "beacon of hope" and showcase its achievements to the world when it holds the 2000 Olympics. Page 1.

Federal Coalition backbenchers have forced Communications Minister Richard Alston to tighten controls covering the overhead cable roll-out of Optus and Telstra. In a bid to quell growing community concern about the cable program, from July 1
next year the installation of new aerial cables will be banned without the agreement of local or State authorities. Page 1.

Australian secondary school students have outperformed their peers from the United States, Germany and Canada in a major international comparison of mathematics and science. Although highest in the English speaking world, our 13-year olds ranked fifth in he area of maths and science after trailing students from Singapore, Korea and Japan. Page 1.

New South Wales Premier Bob Carr has crushed a caucus revolt over stronger powers that have been granted to the State's new police commissioner, Peter Ryan. At the heat of the dispute were powers allowing Ryan to dismiss members of the State's police servce whom he no longer trusted. Ryan has already drawn up a list of 96 "corrupt" police he intends to remove. Page 2.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales Police Commissioner Peter Ryan, has accused corrupt police officers of devising a plan against his reforms while Premier Bob Carr has forced his backbench into accepting reforms in the State's police force. Ryan claims it is "dishonest" oficers that can be found trying to oppose his anti-corruption push. Page 1.

The New South Wales Government reversed its vow last night to deprive prisoners from claiming from the Victims Compensation Tribunal. To ensure the passage through Parliament of a package of victims' compensation reforms, the Government agreed to
support rights for prisoners' compensation in "special circumstances". Page 2.

The man behind Australia's worst massacre, Port Arthur gunman Martin Bryant, will eventually be placed with other maximum-security prisoners according to the Tasmanian Attorney-General Ray Groom. Chief Justice William Cox will sentence Bryant this morning after Bryant pleaded guilty to 72 charges, including 35 of murder. Page 3.

According to new traffic assessments prepared by the Roads and Traffic Authority, traffic volume is expected to almost triple along some parts of Sydney's proposed A$600 million Eastern Distributor extension. Some parts of the city's inner-east are expectd to attract over 125,000 cars each day within 10 years of the tollway's planned completion in June 2000. Page 3.
THE AGE

The Speaker of the Victorian Legislative Assembly, Jim Plowman, has put himself on a collision course with the Kennett Government over his comments yesterday that the auditor-general needed to be kept independent and should advise Parliament without fear or favour. The comments came during a debate on the Kennett Government's attempts to bypass the watchdog. Page A1.

Chief police commissioner Neil Comrie and Ombudsman Dr Barry Perry yesterday personally removed a senior official at the Ombudsman's office, after it was revealed that she had a secret personal relationship with a high-ranking police officer while
she was ivestigating corruption allegations against police. Page A1.

Overall Australia's 13-year-olds have ranked in the top ten for both maths and science in the world's largest maths and science survey. The top ranks of each field were dominated by Asian nations, with Australia fifth in science and ninth in maths. Page A2.

Thousands of teachers, parents and students protested yesterday in a march to the Victorian Parliament to complain about the plight of Victorian Government schools. The rally's speakers said the Government was letting the Victorian education system down wth Budget cuts and the proposal for up to 113 schools to be closed or merge. Page A2.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
